findings: Truncated EMA grid has substantially clearer faces than early checkpoints, with visible clerical collars and bare heads.
Several samples retain ghosted eyes or glasses-like bands, especially first row first column and third row third column.
Most faces still share a narrow range of dark hair, face shape and complexion; this fixed grid cannot establish unseen-latent identity diversity.
Untruncated grid exposes further distortions in collars, shoulders, hair and facial features; apparent eyewear sits above one head.
decision: Continue bounded CDC comparison; no production promotion. Prepare geometry-preserving paired-edit data experiment independently.
